fort-st-john-plateau.name: Highway Camp
fort-st-john-plateau.description: The staging area where Highway 97 meets the access road. Last chance for civilization.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Pipeline Crossing
fort-st-john-plateau.description: The road crosses over the main gas pipeline. Heavy truck traffic.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block FJ-03 - Muskeg Flats
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Black spruce and tamarack on peat, with a pine island the cruise plots will live on. Stray off the ribbon and the ground swallows a boot.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Doig River Camp
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Camp near Doig River First Nation territory. The referral coordinator knows the crew is out here.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block FJ-05 - Spruce Ridge
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Dense white spruce climbing a steep ridge. The boundary follows the break above a gully full of deadfall.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block FJ-06 - Plateau Top
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Open aspen-spruce on the plateau top. Wind howls across the exposed ground and every ribbon needs two knots.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: A-7 Landing
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Active cutblock with equipment staging. Resupply possible from the logging crew.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block FJ-08 - Wetland Bypass
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Mixedwood bench wrapped around a sensitive wetland. The riparian reserve will eat a third of the gross area.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Gas Well Access
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Industrial access road serving several gas wells. Watch for tanker trucks.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block FJ-10 - North Muskeg
fort-st-john-plateau.description: More peatland with a pine-spruce ridge running through it. Someone got a Cat stuck on the approach last spring.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Caribou Flats
fort-st-john-plateau.description: Open area frequented by caribou herds. Tread carefully during migration.

fort-st-john-plateau.name: Block A-12 - End of Road
fort-st-john-plateau.description: The last block on the file, at the end of the road. Time to set up base camp and walk it properly.

muskwa-foothills.name: Fort Nelson Staging
muskwa-foothills.description: The last town before wilderness. Stock up while you can.

muskwa-foothills.name: Block MK-02 - Highway Bench
muskwa-foothills.description: Aspen-spruce mixedwood on the bench just off the Alaska Highway. Wildlife crossing signs every kilometre for a reason.

muskwa-foothills.name: Prophet River
muskwa-foothills.description: Major river crossing on a steel bridge. Check the inspection tag and the water before committing a loaded truck.

muskwa-foothills.name: Foothills Camp
muskwa-foothills.description: Entering the foothills. Terrain gets rougher from here.

muskwa-foothills.name: Block MK-05 - Permafrost Flats
muskwa-foothills.description: Black spruce over discontinuous permafrost. The ground shifts and heaves; the road surface is unpredictable.

muskwa-foothills.name: Block MK-06 - Caribou Corridor
muskwa-foothills.description: Pine-lichen flats inside a boreal caribou corridor. The GAR order and the UWR will shape everything the layout does here.

muskwa-foothills.name: Mountain Pass
muskwa-foothills.description: Steep climb through a narrow pass. No room for error.

muskwa-foothills.name: Alpine Meadow
muskwa-foothills.description: Brief respite in a high alpine meadow. Beautiful but exposed.

muskwa-foothills.name: Remote Camp Alpha
muskwa-foothills.description: Helicopter-supplied remote camp. Limited resupply possible.

muskwa-foothills.name: Block MK-10 - Grizzly Creek
muskwa-foothills.description: Spruce-fir on both sides of a cobble creek the road fords. Named for obvious reasons. Stay alert.

muskwa-foothills.name: Final Ridge
muskwa-foothills.description: Last climb before the destination. Crew is getting tired.

muskwa-foothills.name: Block MK-12 - Muskwa Summit
muskwa-foothills.description: The most remote block in the district: subalpine fir and spruce on a bench nobody has cruised in twenty years.

bulkley-valley.name: Smithers Yard
bulkley-valley.description: Mill yard on the edge of Smithers. Hudson Bay Mountain looms above town like a postcard.

bulkley-valley.name: Telkwa River Bridge
bulkley-valley.description: Single-lane log bridge over the Telkwa. The timbers creak under a loaded truck.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-03 - Ranch Gate
bulkley-valley.description: Aspen-pine on the ranch interface. Close the gate behind you or hear about it later; the range tenure holder will want the fence line respected.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-04 - Cas Yikh Bench
bulkley-valley.description: Hemlock-spruce bench in Cas Yikh house territory. Bark-stripped cedar along the old trail; the House group expects notice before ribbon goes up.

bulkley-valley.name: Birch Bench Camp
bulkley-valley.description: Crew camp tucked into a stand of paper birch. Good water from the creek below.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-06 - VQO Ridgeline
bulkley-valley.description: This ridge is visible from Highway 16. Every boundary bend matters for the visual quality objective.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-07 - Water Intake Buffer
bulkley-valley.description: Community water intake 200 m downslope. Sediment control is not optional here; the streams will all class high.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-08 - Spruce-Birch Mixedwood
bulkley-valley.description: Classic SBSmc2 stand. Hybrid spruce and birch fighting for canopy position in every gap.

bulkley-valley.name: Decker Lake Road Junction
bulkley-valley.description: FSR junction with a fuel cache and radio repeater. Contractor trucks resupply here.

bulkley-valley.name: Morice River Overlook
bulkley-valley.description: The road climbs above the Morice valley. Coho spawning channels glint silver far below.

bulkley-valley.name: Foggy Bench
bulkley-valley.description: Valley fog pools here most mornings. Visibility under 50 m until it burns off by ten.

bulkley-valley.name: Block BV-12 - Escarpment Edge
bulkley-valley.description: The last block on the file, perched on the Bulkley escarpment. The view is worth the drive, which is exactly the problem for the VQO.

fraser-plateau.name: Hixon Staging
fraser-plateau.description: Gravel lot south of Prince George where the crew musters. Coffee from the gas station across the road.

fraser-plateau.name: Blackwater Road
fraser-plateau.description: Long straight FSR through beetle-killed pine. Grey snags line both sides like a dead army.

fraser-plateau.name: Block FP-03 - Blackwater Salvage
fraser-plateau.description: Beetle-killed pine salvage off the Blackwater Road. Grey snags over a spruce-fir understorey worth keeping, and a small S4 threading the middle.

fraser-plateau.name: Lheidli T'enneh Camp
fraser-plateau.description: Camp at the edge of Lheidli T'enneh traditional territory. Guardians run a collaborative monitoring program out of here.

fraser-plateau.name: Block FP-05 - Bobtail Bench
fraser-plateau.description: SBSwk1 spruce-fir on a gentle bench above the first-wave plantations. Moose sign everywhere; the wetland on the east edge will need a reserve.

fraser-plateau.name: Dry Creek Gully
fraser-plateau.description: A seasonal creek bed that turns into a washout after rain. The culvert is undersized and the fill above it is soft.

fraser-plateau.name: Block FP-07 - Dry Creek
fraser-plateau.description: Pine-spruce on the hilly ground above Dry Creek. The creek is an S6 most of the year and an S3 for a fortnight each spring; classify it on what the banks say, not the water.

fraser-plateau.name: Wildfire Guard Station
fraser-plateau.description: BC Wildfire Service forward cache. Fuel, water, and a sat phone if things go sideways.

fraser-plateau.name: Block FP-09 - Aspen Blowdown
fraser-plateau.description: A winter windstorm flattened this aspen-spruce stand. Salvage block: root wads, jackstrawed stems, and a lot of ribbon hung at eye level.

fraser-plateau.name: Nazko Road Junction
fraser-plateau.description: Where the main FSR meets the Nazko road. Occasional ranch traffic and dust clouds.

fraser-plateau.name: Block FP-11 - Resilience Trial
fraser-plateau.description: The last block on the file, inside a wildfire resilience trial area. Mixed-species retention and fuel breaks are part of the prescription before the boundary is even walked.

skeena-nass.name: Terrace Log Sort
skeena-nass.description: Sorting yard on the Skeena floodplain. Rain drips off everything. Always.

skeena-nass.name: Skeena River Crossing
skeena-nass.description: Steel bridge over the grey-green Skeena. Spring freshet can close this for days.

skeena-nass.name: Block SN-03 - Hemlock Canyon
skeena-nass.description: Deep-cut canyon draped in old western hemlock. Moss hangs a metre thick from every branch and the terrain stability field card will run to two pages.

skeena-nass.name: Gitanyow Checkpoint
skeena-nass.description: Gitanyow forest stewardship checkpoint. The Guardians check the crew in and confirm which sites are off limits.

skeena-nass.name: Block SN-05 - Karst Bench
skeena-nass.description: Hemlock-cedar over limestone karst with sinkholes and disappearing streams. Watch your step off the ribbon; every sink gets a reserve.

skeena-nass.name: Salmon Creek Crossing
skeena-nass.description: Class A fish stream with coho and steelhead, forded by the road at the riffle. In-stream work window is July 15 to August 31. Period.

skeena-nass.name: Block SN-07 - Redcedar Bottom
skeena-nass.description: Valley-bottom redcedar so thick sunlight barely reaches the ground. Cathedral-quiet, and half the big cedar carries old bark-strip scars.

skeena-nass.name: Nass Camp
skeena-nass.description: Nisga'a Lisims Government liaison camp at the head of the Nass valley. Resupply by truck weekly.

skeena-nass.name: Fog Ridge
skeena-nass.description: Coastal fog banks roll in from the west and stall on this ridge. Visibility can drop to zero.

skeena-nass.name: Block SN-10 - Spruce-Hemlock Bluffs
skeena-nass.description: Sitka spruce and hemlock on exposed bluffs above the river. Wind-shaped crowns lean inland; the windthrow risk will drive the boundary.

skeena-nass.name: Lava Bed Flats
skeena-nass.description: Nisga'a Memorial Lava Bed edges the road. Volcanic rock and thin soils make for rough going.

skeena-nass.name: Block SN-12 - Nass Headwaters
skeena-nass.description: The last block on the file, in the upper Nass. Rain-soaked CWH at its finest. Bring an extra dry bag for the field cards.

tahltan-highland.name: Dease Lake Yard
tahltan-highland.description: Contractor yard at Dease Lake. The fuel truck comes twice a month if the road holds.

tahltan-highland.name: Telegraph Creek Road
tahltan-highland.description: Notorious single-lane public road carved into canyon walls. Switchbacks with 500 m drops.

tahltan-highland.name: Stikine River Crossing
tahltan-highland.description: Reaction ferry across the Stikine. Current runs fast with glacial melt. Ferry shuts at dusk.

tahltan-highland.name: Tahltan Village Camp
tahltan-highland.description: Camp near the Tahltan village. Elders walk the cedar harvest boundaries with the crew each season.

tahltan-highland.name: Block TH-05 - Moraine Bench
tahltan-highland.description: Spruce-pine on unstable glacial till left by a retreating glacier. Boulders shift without warning; the terrain stability notes will decide the road location.

tahltan-highland.name: Block TH-06 - Subalpine Parkland
tahltan-highland.description: Sparse Engelmann spruce and subalpine fir in wind-blasted parkland. Tree line is close and the stocking standards will be an argument.

tahltan-highland.name: Block TH-07 - Ealue Lake
tahltan-highland.description: Fly-in block on Ealue Lake with a supply cache on the shore. The bush plane drops gear when the ceiling lifts; the lakeshore reserve will be wide.

tahltan-highland.name: Willow Scrub Plateau
tahltan-highland.description: Dense willow and dwarf birch across a windswept plateau. Grizzly country through and through.

tahltan-highland.name: Outburst Channel
tahltan-highland.description: Glacial lake outburst flood channel. The last event stripped the road to bedrock and the replacement culvert is already undersized.

tahltan-highland.name: Wolverine Pass
tahltan-highland.description: High pass above tree line. Snow possible any month. Named after the residents, not the comic book.

tahltan-highland.name: Block TH-11 - Highland Bench
tahltan-highland.description: The last block on the file, on a subarctic bench. The most remote timber in the province, bar none.
